discovery: Spectroscopic detection and characterisation of exoplanet atmospheres

nominees.name: David Charbonneau
nominees.affiliation: Harvard University / Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian, USA

motivation: These three physicists turned planets around other stars from points in orbital diagrams into physical objects with measurable chemistry. Seager (with Sasselov, 2000) calculated how atomic and molecular absorption imprints on starlight filtering through a transiting planet's atmosphere. Charbonneau detected the first exoplanet transit (HD 209458b, 1999) and, in 2002, the first exoplanet atmosphere through sodium absorption. Snellen pioneered ground-based high-resolution cross-correlation spectroscopy, detecting CO in a planet's atmosphere, measuring its orbital motion and the first planetary winds (2010), and later its spin. Together, these techniques underpin the detection of water, CO2, SO2 and other molecules with Hubble and JWST. They allow us to test photochemistry, disequilibrium chemistry and the elemental ratios inherited from planet-forming discs. This work opened a new observational window that joins molecular physics to the origin and diversity of planetary systems.
